articles.title: Ralph Lauren proves the American dream still sells at New York fashion week
articles.summary: Designer mixes burnt-out velvet and shredded denim with a mythology that keeps getting more profitable. The opening show of fashion’s month of catwalks was not on the official schedule, but Viola Davis and Cynthia Erivo were snuggled on to celebrity-packed benches in a cathedral-sized marble hall…
body: Ralph Lauren, 86, took his bow at the end of this women’s wear show casually dressed in a varsity jacket spelling out New York. In an industry obsessed with youth and novelty, Lauren is more relevant than ever in his ninth decade.

He described the show as “irreverent”. Velvet evening wear was burnt out to show a little skin beneath. There were shredded, low-slung jeans – take note, jeans-wearers everywhere – and a wink to the extra-wide ties that started his empire 59 years ago.
The spray-painted brocade gowns and lush embroidered evening coats on this catwalk will be giddily expensive, but the energy propelling the brand comes from a much broader audience.

Gen Z has rediscovered Ralph Lauren, and its Polo shirts, rugby shirts and baseball caps are cool again, a renaissance that shows up emphatically on the balance sheet. This year the fashion house reached its highest ever annual revenue figure of $8.1bn (£6bn) – a rise of 15% on the previous year.

articles.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for a not-sachertorte | A kitchen in Rome
articles.summary: A chocolate cake inspired by the Sacher hotel in Vienna’s trademark creation and emulated by a local Roman pasticceria. This column began two years ago, almost to the day, when I made a birthday cake for a friend. “I don’t mind,” was her reply when I first asked what sort of cake she would like.
body: Barberini is a local bar and cake shop, and the mini cakes she was referring to are their sacher (inspired by sachertorte, of course) – chocolate sponge cakes with a heart of apricot jam and a glossy, chocolate glaze. At Barberini, each one is the size of a single draughts piece, but deep, so not quite two bites but slightly too big for one, unless you open your mouth very wide. “You mean sachertorte?” I said. “That would be great,” was her reply, before changing the subject to I can’t remember what. Walking home, I regretted asking.

According to the Sacher hotel website, its sachertorte (perhaps the world’s most famous cake) is still handmade using Franz Sacher’s original recipe. It also provides a recipe – a wonderful, quite complicated, anxiety-inducing recipe. It is also an approximate one, with a note in capital letters and highlighted red explaining that the original recipe must remain a tightly kept secret. I have never felt so relieved at not being given a recipe.

articles.title: ‘Scots are the kindest people on earth!’ Meet the Americans moving to Scotland
articles.summary: Since Donald Trump’s re-election in 2024, there has been a 63% rise in Americans renting properties in Scotland. Politics is one reason – but there are many other surprising motivations … Four years ago, when Tammi Gaw, a 50-year-old property adviser, moved from Washington DC to Glasgow with her…
body: They are not alone. According to data from Rightmove, 28% of inquiries from Americans about buying a home in the UK are about Scotland, a larger number than for London. And a recent survey from lettings platform Goodlord reported a 63% rise in the number of Americans renting properties in Scotland since Donald Trump’s re-election in November 2024.

But Gaw, a member of Democrats Abroad, believes that disenchantment with the current administration does not fully explain Scotland’s appeal. She also cites the feelgood factor created by the more than 20,000 Scottish football fans who descended on Massachusetts for the World Cup this summer, winning over Bostonians with their pranks and bagpipe parades, enriching local bar owners and even bagging up their rubbish: “The Tartan Army put on a better marketing campaign for their country than any funded programme by the government. People now view Scotland as a very fun option.”

There are other, more hard-headed reasons for Scotland’s allure. “I advise people across all income brackets,” says Gaw. “Some are planning ahead. For example, they want Scottish residency so that, later, their children can get free university tuition fees.”

articles.title: Meet the New FDA-Approved Sunscreen Filter Bemotrizinol
articles.summary: On June 10, 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new sunscreen filter, its first in over 20 years: bemotrizinol. Here, experts break down the game-changing ingredient and all its benefits.
body: Any beauty lover knows there’s one must-visit location when traveling overseas: The pharmacy. European, Australian, and Asian sunscreens are also known for their special formulations, sunscreen filters, and more. And for the longest time, US-regulated sunscreen has gotten a bad rap for being outdated and lackluster formula-wise compared to its international counterparts. That is, until now. Earlier this summer, the US Food & Drug Administration (FDA) finally approved a new sunscreen filter that could signal the start of better sunscreen innovation in the States: bemotrizinol (BEMT).

“The agency’s action to add bemotrizinol as an active ingredient to the sunscreen OTC monograph marks the first time in 20 years that a new sunscreen active ingredient has become available to US consumers,” a spokesperson for the FDA tells Vogue. “It also represents the first industry-initiated administrative order to be finalized under the landmark OTC monograph reform legislation enacted in 2020.”

articles.summary: As the 2026 Venice Film Festival kicks off this week, all eyes will be on the red carpet—with the likes of George and Amal Clooney, Claire Foy, and Robert Pattinson arriving in the Italian city. See all the best fashion from Venice Film Festival so far.
body: Red carpet lovers, it’s your lucky day: The 2026 Venice Film Festival has officially arrived.

The film roster for this year’s festival has plenty of buzzy projects to take in: Among them is Martin McDonagh’s Oscar-tipped black comedy Wild Horse Nine; Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime; a Robert Pattinson-led portrait of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen; and Bunker, Florian Zeller’s marital drama starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Better year, however, is what all of these A-listers will be wearing on the step and repeat for the splashy premieres. This is, after all, the festival that last year offered the first glimpses of new-era Chanel, Dior, Versace and Bottega Veneta before their respective runway debuts, and which has given us Lady Gaga’s feathered Valentino couture gown in 2018 and Zendaya’s wet-look Balmain dress in 2021, among other standout moments.

articles.title: 25+ Best Suede Jackets for Fall 2026
articles.summary: The best suede jackets are still trending, and the options are endless. Set aside your leather jackets in favor of suede blazers, cropped styles and trenches.
body: When it comes to quintessential transitional style, outerwear in leather, denim, and cotton gabardine is a given. But the resurrection of the suede jacket, over the past few years, has been hard to miss.

Suede jackets made their mark on the fall runways, from Altuzarra’s cropped, buttoned-up style to Burberry’s shearling lined overcoats—all feel perfectly suited to the chiller months ahead. Previous collections also proved that suede can come take on unexpected colorways: Gabriela Hearst showcased sumptuous deep blue suiting, while Alberta Ferretti explored oversized blazers in a rich burnt orange hue.

Of course, it’s a jacket the really comes into its on own during Fashion Month, where its versatility is on full display in the street style we see outside the shows. Its styling possibilities run the gamut, from pairing seamlessly with printed silk pants and crimson sweaters —as Chloe Malle demonstrated during last season’s NYFW—to contrasting sweet, airy dresses for an unexpected take on transitional dressing.

articles.title: Will the iPad Ever Be a Worthy Mac Replacement?
articles.summary: Welcome to a new series called Apple a Day, where sites in the CNET family are sharing pieces of Apple content from our archives—an article, review and/or video—daily from now through late September.
body: For the first five years of its life, the iPad could only run one app at a time. Then, iOS 9 changed everything. That update, released 10 years ago this month, introduced multitasking to the Apple tablet for the first time. "Split View" let you run two apps side-by-side at once; "Slide Over" gave you quick access to a third app in an iPhone-style window; and Picture in Picture made it possible to watch a video while working on something else. In an article published at the time, these changes prompted Lifehacker to proclaim that "iOS 9 actually makes the iPad usable for work."

In total, you could have up to four different windows on screen through this concoction of features, a huge improvement over the previous limit of "one." Coupled with the new keyboard shortcuts, iOS 9 transformed the iPad, and brought it closer to the laptop replacement so many users wanted it to be. "Closer" being the key word there.
